correctness.rationale: For a length-ell factor at phase r, the earliest subsequence embedding uses one copy of P plus one for each descent. There are ell-1-floor((r+ell-1)/q) descents. Thus r must be at least A=(q-1)ell-qm+1, and the actual factor starts give 0<=r<=min(q-1,qn-ell). With 1<=ell<=qn, nonemptiness requires just A<=q-1 and A<=qn-ell, respectively equivalent over the integers to ell<=m+ceil(m/(q-1)) and ell<=m+n-1. This proves the length and the entire phase interval directly, including ell=1, n=1 and q=2; different phases have different first letters. The equal-power simplification is valid for q>=3,m>=2, and the alternating two-letter subsequence proves the claimed linear lower bound on the gap. The transition-window proof has a harmless empty-window edge case at t=0 (there need not be a first increasing edge); the interval proof covers it directly. Independently, for q=3,m=n=2 the only optimal factors are 102 and 021. The 567 parameter cells and 70,756 per-factor checks are recorded supporting results, not an independent run or the basis of the theorem.
